/** Insert a new customer in the webERP database. This function takes an
   associative array called $CustomerDetails, where the keys are the
   names of the fields in the debtorsmaster table, and the values are the
   values to insert. The only mandatory fields are the debtorno, name,
   currency code, sales type, payment terms, and reason code
   fields. If the other fields aren't set, then the database defaults
   are used. The function returns an array called $Errors. The database
   is only updated if the $Errors is empty, else the function returns an
   array of one to many error codes.
*/
function InsertCustomer($CustomerDetails, $user = '', $password = '') {
	$Errors = array();
	$db = db($user, $password);
	if (gettype($db)=='integer') {
		$Errors[0]=NoAuthorisation;
		return $Errors;
	}
	foreach ($CustomerDetails as $key => $Value) {
		$CustomerDetails[$key] = DB_escape_string($Value);
	}
	$autonumbersql="SELECT confvalue FROM config
					 WHERE confname='AutoDebtorNo'";
	$autonumberresult=DB_query($autonumbersql);
	$autonumber=DB_fetch_row($autonumberresult);
	if ($autonumber[0]==0) {
		$Errors=VerifyDebtorNo($CustomerDetails['debtorno'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	} else {
		$CustomerDetails['debtorno']='';
	}
	$Errors=VerifyDebtorName($CustomerDetails['name'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['address1'])){
		$Errors=VerifyAddressLine($CustomerDetails['address1'], 40, sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['address2'])){
		$Errors=VerifyAddressLine($CustomerDetails['address2'], 40, sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['address3'])){
		$Errors=VerifyAddressLine($CustomerDetails['address3'], 40, sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['address4'])){
		$Errors=VerifyAddressLine($CustomerDetails['address4'], 50, sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['address5'])){
		$Errors=VerifyAddressLine($CustomerDetails['address5'], 20, sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['address6'])){
		$Errors=VerifyAddressLine($CustomerDetails['address6'], 15, sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['currcode'])){
		$Errors=VerifyCurrencyCode($CustomerDetails['currcode'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['salestype'])){
		$Errors=VerifySalesType($CustomerDetails['salestype'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['clientsince'])){
		$Errors=VerifyClientSince($CustomerDetails['clientsince'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['holdreason'])){
		$Errors=VerifyHoldReason($CustomerDetails['holdreason'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['paymentterms'])){
		$Errors=VerifyPaymentTerms($CustomerDetails['paymentterms'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['discount'])){
		$Errors=VerifyDiscount($CustomerDetails['discount'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['pymtdiscount'])){
		$Errors=VerifyPymtDiscount($CustomerDetails['pymtdiscount'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['lastpaid'])){
		$Errors=VerifyLastPaid($CustomerDetails['lastpaid'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['lastpaiddate'])){
		$Errors=VerifyLastPaidDate($CustomerDetails['lastpaiddate'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['creditlimit'])){
		$Errors=VerifyCreditLimit($CustomerDetails['creditlimit'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['invaddrbranch'])){
		$Errors=VerifyInvAddrBranch($CustomerDetails['invaddrbranch'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['discountcode'])){
		$Errors=VerifyDiscountCode($CustomerDetails['discountcode'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['ediinvoices'])){

	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['ediorders'])){

	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['edireference'])){
		$Errors=VerifyEDIReference($CustomerDetails['edireference'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['editransport'])){
		$Errors=VerifyEDITransport($CustomerDetails['editransport'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['ediserveruser'])){
		$Errors=VerifyEDIServerUser($CustomerDetails['ediserveruser'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['ediserverpwd'])){
		$Errors=VerifyEDIServerPassword($CustomerDetails['ediserverpwd'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['taxref'])){
		$Errors=VerifyTaxRef($CustomerDetails['taxref'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['customerpoline'])){
		$Errors=VerifyCustomerPOLine($CustomerDetails['customerpoline'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['typeid'])){
		$Errors=VerifyCustomerType($CustomerDetails['typeid'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
	}
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['nextreviewdate'])){
		$Errors=VerifyNextReviewDate($CustomerDetails['nextreviewdate'], sizeof($Errors), $Errors);
		if ($CustomerDetails['nextreviewdate'] === '') {
			unset($CustomerDetails['nextreviewdate']);
		}
	}
	/* Credit control: a new customer cannot be created on hold or watch, only the credit controller can do that */
	if (isset($CustomerDetails['holdreason']) and sizeof($Errors) == 0 and CreditHoldReasonRestricted($CustomerDetails['holdreason'])) {
		$Errors[sizeof($Errors)] = CreditControlRestricted;
	}
	$FieldNames='';
	$FieldValues='';

		$FieldNames.=$key.', ';
		$FieldValues.='"'.$Value.'", ';

	  'VALUES ('.mb_substr($FieldValues,0,-2).') ';
	if (sizeof($Errors)==0) {
		$Result = DB_query($SQL);
		if (DB_error_no() != 0) {
			$Errors[0] = DatabaseUpdateFailed;
		} else {
			$Errors[0]=0;
		}
	}
	return $Errors;
}

<?php

/* Shared functions for customer credit control: holds, reviews, reminders, late payment charges
and bad debt write-offs.

Transaction types used in debtortrans (see sql/updates/44.php):
	13 - late payment charge (a debit, like an invoice)
	14 - bad debt write-off (a credit, like a credit note)
*/

define('CREDIT_TRANS_CHARGE', 13);
define('CREDIT_TRANS_WRITEOFF', 14);

/* Security token held by the credit controller and deputy */
define('CREDIT_CONTROLLER_TOKEN', 21);

/* holdreasons.dissallowinvoices: 0 = invoicing ok, 1 = account on hold, 2 = account on watch */
define('CREDIT_HOLD_NONE', 0);
define('CREDIT_HOLD_BLOCKED', 1);
define('CREDIT_HOLD_WATCH', 2);

/**
 * True when the logged in user may put accounts on hold, release them, change limits, send reminders, charge
 * late payment charges and write off bad debt.
 */
function CreditControllerAccess() {
	return isset($_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens'])
		and is_array($_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens'])
		and in_array(CREDIT_CONTROLLER_TOKEN, $_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens']);
}

/**
 * The invoicing status of a customer's account straight from the database:
 * 0 invoicing ok, 1 on hold (no invoicing), 2 on watch (warn only). Unknown customers return 0.
 */
function GetCustomerHoldStatus($DebtorNo) {
	$SQL = "SELECT holdreasons.dissallowinvoices
			FROM debtorsmaster
			INNER JOIN holdreasons
				ON debtorsmaster.holdreason = holdreasons.reasoncode
			WHERE debtorsmaster.debtorno = '" . DB_escape_string($DebtorNo) . "'";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return CREDIT_HOLD_NONE;
	}
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	return (int) $MyRow[0];
}

/** True if the hold reason puts an account on hold or on watch (anything but plain "invoicing ok") */
function CreditHoldReasonRestricted($HoldReason) {
	$SQL = "SELECT dissallowinvoices FROM holdreasons WHERE reasoncode = '" . DB_escape_string($HoldReason) . "'";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	return $MyRow and (int) $MyRow[0] != CREDIT_HOLD_NONE;
}

/**
 * SQL restricting a query to the customers of the logged in sales person. Empty for everyone else.
 * $DebtorColumn is the (qualified) debtorno column of the query.
 */
function CreditSalesmanCustomerSQL($DebtorColumn) {
	if (isset($_SESSION['SalesmanLogin']) and $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] != '') {
		return " AND " . $DebtorColumn . " IN (SELECT debtorno
				FROM custbranch
				WHERE salesman = '" . DB_escape_string($_SESSION['SalesmanLogin']) . "') ";
	}
	return '';
}

/**
 * SQL restricting debtortrans rows to those of the logged in sales person. Empty for everyone else.
 */
function CreditSalesmanTransSQL($TransAlias = 'debtortrans') {
	if (isset($_SESSION['SalesmanLogin']) and $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] != '') {
		return " AND " . $TransAlias . ".salesperson = '" . DB_escape_string($_SESSION['SalesmanLogin']) . "' ";
	}
	return '';
}

/**
 * The debtorno of the customer a customer-login user belongs to, or '' if the user is not a customer login.
 * Read from the users table rather than the session, as the session CustomerID can be changed on the search page.
 */
function CreditCustomerLoginDebtorNo() {
	$SQL = "SELECT customerid FROM www_users WHERE userid = '" . DB_escape_string($_SESSION['UserID']) . "'";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	return $MyRow ? trim($MyRow[0]) : '';
}

/**
 * SQL boolean expression (MySQL) which is true when the invoice row is "past due" at the given level.
 *   level 1 - past due, level 2 - first overdue band (PastDueDays1), level 3 - second overdue band (PastDueDays2)
 * These are the very same tests as the aged debtors report, customer inquiry and customer statement use
 * for their "Past Due", first and second overdue columns - keep them identical.
 * $Trans is the alias of debtortrans, $Terms the alias of paymentterms.
 */
function CreditPastDueSQL($Level, $Trans = 'debtortrans', $Terms = 'paymentterms') {
	$Days = 0;
	if ($Level == 2) {
		$Days = (int) $_SESSION['PastDueDays1'];
	} elseif ($Level == 3) {
		$Days = (int) $_SESSION['PastDueDays2'];
	}
	if ($Level == 1) {
		return "(CASE WHEN " . $Terms . ".daysbeforedue > 0
				THEN
					CASE WHEN (TO_DAYS(Now()) - TO_DAYS(" . $Trans . ".trandate)) >= " . $Terms . ".daysbeforedue
					THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
				ELSE
					CASE WHEN TO_DAYS(Now()) - TO_DAYS(ADDDATE(last_day(" . $Trans . ".trandate), " . $Terms . ".dayinfollowingmonth)) >= 0
					THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
				END)";
	}
	return "(CASE WHEN " . $Terms . ".daysbeforedue > 0
			THEN
				CASE WHEN (TO_DAYS(Now()) - TO_DAYS(" . $Trans . ".trandate)) > " . $Terms . ".daysbeforedue
					AND TO_DAYS(Now()) - TO_DAYS(" . $Trans . ".trandate) >= (" . $Terms . ".daysbeforedue + " . $Days . ")
				THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
			ELSE
				CASE WHEN TO_DAYS(Now()) - TO_DAYS(ADDDATE(last_day(" . $Trans . ".trandate), " . $Terms . ".dayinfollowingmonth)) >= " . $Days . "
				THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
			END)";
}

/** SQL expression giving the reminder level (0 = not past due, 1, 2 or 3) of an invoice row */
function CreditReminderLevelSQL($Trans = 'debtortrans', $Terms = 'paymentterms') {
	return "(CASE WHEN " . CreditPastDueSQL(3, $Trans, $Terms) . " = 1 THEN 3
				WHEN " . CreditPastDueSQL(2, $Trans, $Terms) . " = 1 THEN 2
				WHEN " . CreditPastDueSQL(1, $Trans, $Terms) . " = 1 THEN 1
				ELSE 0 END)";
}

/** The date (SQL format) a review done on $FromDate (SQL format, default today) should be followed up */
function CreditDefaultNextReviewDate($FromDate = '') {
	if ($FromDate == '') {
		$FromDate = date('Y-m-d');
	}
	$Months = (int) ($_SESSION['CreditReviewIntervalMonths'] ?? 12);
	if ($Months < 1) {
		$Months = 12;
	}
	return date('Y-m-d', strtotime($FromDate . ' +' . $Months . ' months'));
}

/** True if $Date is a valid date in SQL format (YYYY-MM-DD) */
function CreditIsSQLDate($Date) {
	if (!is_string($Date) or !preg_match('/^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/', $Date, $Parts)) {
		return false;
	}
	return checkdate((int) $Parts[2], (int) $Parts[3], (int) $Parts[1]);
}

/** The outcomes a credit review can have, keyed by the value stored in creditreviews.outcome */
function CreditReviewOutcomes() {
	return array(
		'keep' => __('Limit kept'),
		'raise' => __('Limit raised'),
		'lower' => __('Limit lowered'),
		'hold' => __('Account put on hold'),
		'watch' => __('Account put on watch'),
		'release' => __('Account released from hold')
	);
}

/** The reminder levels */
function CreditReminderLevels() {
	return array(
		1 => __('Friendly reminder'),
		2 => __('Firm reminder'),
		3 => __('Final notice')
	);
}

/**
 * Returns the email addresses of the contacts of a customer who receive statements
 * (custcontacts.statement = 1) and have a valid address
 */
function CreditStatementContacts($DebtorNo) {
	$Emails = array();
	$SQL = "SELECT contactname, email
			FROM custcontacts
			WHERE debtorno = '" . DB_escape_string($DebtorNo) . "'
			AND statement = 1
			AND email <> ''";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	while ($MyRow = DB_fetch_array($Result)) {
		if (IsEmailAddress($MyRow['email'])) {
			$Emails[$MyRow['email']] = $MyRow['contactname'];
		}
	}
	return $Emails;
}

/**
 * Records a movement of the debtors control account and the other side in gltrans, in the functional
 * currency. Positive $Amount debits $DebitAccount, credits $CreditAccount. Returns nothing, errors roll back
 * the transaction and stop the script (DB_query with the transaction flag).
 * The last gltrans row inserted is the one tagged by InsertGLTags, so tags are inserted for the debit line
 * when the income/expense account is the one that carries them.
 */
function CreditPostGL($Type, $TransNo, $SQLDate, $PeriodNo, $Account, $Narrative, $Amount, $Tags = array()) {
	$SQL = "INSERT INTO gltrans (type,
								typeno,
								trandate,
								periodno,
								account,
								narrative,
								amount)
			VALUES ('" . $Type . "',
					'" . $TransNo . "',
					'" . $SQLDate . "',
					'" . $PeriodNo . "',
					'" . $Account . "',
					'" . DB_escape_string(mb_substr($Narrative, 0, 200)) . "',
					'" . $Amount . "')";
	DB_query($SQL, __('Cannot insert a GL entry because'), '', true);
	if (!empty($Tags)) {
		InsertGLTags($Tags);
	}
}

input.content:
Customer Credit Control

Credit control in webERP applies the same rules every time, by everybody, and leaves a trail the auditors can follow. It covers credit reviews, holding and releasing accounts, overdue reminders, late payment charges and the write-off of bad debt. The screens are on the Receivables menus. Only the credit controller and the deputy - the users whose security role holds the security token Credit control - reviews, holds, reminders, charges and write-offs (token 21) - can change anything. A new database gives the token to the System Administrator role; give it to the role of the credit controller in the Access Permissions Maintenance screen. Everyone else with access to customers can look at the credit status, the reviews and the history but not change them.

Sales people who log in see credit information only for their own customers and their own transactions in every list and report described here. Customers who log in see their own reminders and charges only, on the screen My Reminders and Charges.

Credit Reviews

Every trade customer is reviewed at least once a year - large or risky customers more often. Choose Credit Reviews on the Receivables Transactions menu or follow the link on the customer page. A review records the date, the user who is logged in, the outcome, the new limit where it changes, the date the next review is due and the comments. The comments can run to several paragraphs; quotes from the customer's emails can be pasted in. The outcome is one of:

  • Limit kept
  • Limit raised - enter the new, higher limit
  • Limit lowered - enter the new, lower limit
  • Account put on hold - choose the credit status to give it, it must be a status that disallows invoicing
  • Account put on watch - staff are warned, but can carry on
  • Account released from hold - choose a credit status that allows invoicing

When a review changes the limit or the credit status the customer's account is changed in the same database transaction as the review is saved. If either part fails neither is saved. Comments must be entered whenever the limit or the status changes, so that the history always shows why. The next review date is set by the review (the default is the company setting Credit Review Interval months ahead) and is shown on the customer page; it can also be entered when a customer is created. A customer that has never been reviewed has no date and is listed as never reviewed in the report.

A review entered by mistake can be corrected with the button Entered by mistake and a reason. The review stays in the history marked as a mistake, together with who corrected it and why, but it does not undo the change that was made to the account - record a new review to put the limit or the status right.

Credit History

From the customer page, Credit reviews, reminders and charges shows the past reviews newest first, the reminders that have been sent with the invoices each included, the late payment charges and the bad debt write-offs of the customer.

Credit Reviews Due Report

The report lists customers whose review is overdue, never done, or due within the number of days that you choose, with their balance, the overdue amount (invoices past due), the credit limit, the credit still available (the limit less the balance and the value of outstanding orders, as used at order entry) and the date they last paid. The report can be printed as PDF.

Holding and Releasing Accounts

Each customer has a credit status (see the section on credit status ratings). A status can allow invoicing, put the account on watch, or put it on hold. An account on hold gets no new invoices by any route: orders keyed by staff, recurring orders (the template is left untouched and is picked up again once the hold is released), electronic (EDI) orders, orders and invoices created through the web connection (API) and the invoicing of orders that were entered before the hold. An account on watch lets staff carry on but warns them. When an order would take a customer over the credit limit, what happens follows the company setting Check Credit Limits and nothing in credit control overrides it.

Only the credit controller can put an account on hold, release it or change the limit; on the customer maintenance screen the credit limit, status and review date are shown but disabled to everyone else. Neither can the web connection change them.

Overdue Reminders

There are three reminder levels: a friendly reminder once an invoice is past due, a firm reminder at the first overdue band and a final notice at the second overdue band. The bands are the number of days of the company settings First Overdue Deadline and Second Overdue Deadline, and "past due" means exactly what the invoice, the statement, the customer inquiry and the aged debtors report call past due. The wording of each letter is in the system parameters. Customers on hold get the final notice wording.

On the screen Overdue Reminders you see who would get which level, you can untick anyone you want to leave out, and then you send. Each reminder is a PDF letter on the company letterhead emailed to the contacts of the customer who receive statements. If the customer has no such contact, or the email fails, the letter is not counted as sent and the customer is listed among the reminders not sent. A customer never gets the same level twice for the same invoices, even if the run is repeated: an invoice is reminded again only when it has reached a higher level. The reminders sent are on the customer's credit history page.

Late Payment Charges

At month end the credit controller may charge interest on the invoices that are past due at the rate per month set in the system parameters, and a fixed reminder fee for each final notice sent that month (a letter with the final notice wording, which includes the ones to customers on hold). Nothing is charged until you tick the charges and press the button. The charges are customer transactions in the currency of the customer: they appear on the account, the inquiry and the statement, count in the aged debtors, can be printed and emailed like an invoice and can be matched against payments in the allocation screen. They are posted to the ledger in the same period - debit debtors control and credit the late payment charges income account chosen in the company preferences - and can carry GL tags. Running the charges again for the same month cannot charge twice.

Bad Debt Write-off

Choose the customer, tick the invoices (or late payment charges) with an amount left to pay - the box in the heading selects the whole balance - and enter the reason. The write-off clears the items it covers. It is posted to the bad debt expense account chosen in the company preferences, which can never be a control account, and credits debtors control. For a customer in a foreign currency the difference between the rate of the invoice and the rate of the write-off goes to the sales exchange variances account, the same way as for a payment. The write-off is a customer transaction like the late payment charges.

My Reminders and Charges

A customer who logs in sees the reminders and the late payment charges addressed to the customer, and nobody else's.

Settings

The system parameters hold the credit review interval in months, the late payment interest rate per month, the reminder fee and the wording of the three reminder letters. The company preferences hold the two new ledger accounts, the late payment charges income account and the bad debt expense account; they cannot be deleted in the chart of accounts while they are in use there. A new installation, with or without demo data, has these settings; an existing database gets them from the database upgrade, which runs by itself from the Database Upgrade screen after the new code is installed.

Each customer has a credit status (see the section on credit status ratings). A status can allow invoicing, put the account on watch, or put it on hold. An account on hold gets no new invoices by any route: orders keyed by staff, recurring orders (the template is left untouched and is picked up again once the hold is released), electronic (EDI) orders, orders and invoices created through the web connection (API) and the invoicing of orders that were entered before the hold. An account on watch lets staff carry on but warns them. When an order would take a customer over the credit limit, what happens follows the company setting Check Credit Limits and nothing in credit control overrides it.

Only the credit controller can put an account on hold, release it or change the limit; on the customer maintenance screen the credit limit, status and review date are shown but disabled to everyone else. Neither can the web connection change them.

Overdue Reminders

There are three reminder levels: a friendly reminder once an invoice is past due, a firm reminder at the first overdue band and a final notice at the second overdue band. The bands are the number of days of the company settings First Overdue Deadline and Second Overdue Deadline, and "past due" means exactly what the invoice, the statement, the customer inquiry and the aged debtors report call past due. The wording of each letter is in the system parameters. Customers on hold get the final notice wording.

On the screen Overdue Reminders you see who would get which level, you can untick anyone you want to leave out, and then you send. Each reminder is a PDF letter on the company letterhead emailed to the contacts of the customer who receive statements. If the customer has no such contact, or the email fails, the letter is not counted as sent and the customer is listed among the reminders not sent. A customer never gets the same level twice for the same invoices, even if the run is repeated: an invoice is reminded again only when it has reached a higher level. The reminders sent are on the customer's credit history page.

Late Payment Charges

At month end the credit controller may charge interest on the invoices that are past due at the rate per month set in the system parameters, and a fixed reminder fee for each final notice sent that month (a letter with the final notice wording, which includes the ones to customers on hold). Nothing is charged until you tick the charges and press the button. The charges are customer transactions in the currency of the customer: they appear on the account, the inquiry and the statement, count in the aged debtors, can be printed and emailed like an invoice and can be matched against payments in the allocation screen. They are posted to the ledger in the same period - debit debtors control and credit the late payment charges income account chosen in the company preferences - and can carry GL tags. Running the charges again for the same month cannot charge twice.

Bad Debt Write-off

Choose the customer, tick the invoices (or late payment charges) with an amount left to pay - the box in the heading selects the whole balance - and enter the reason. The write-off clears the items it covers. It is posted to the bad debt expense account chosen in the company preferences, which can never be a control account, and credits debtors control. For a customer in a foreign currency the difference between the rate of the invoice and the rate of the write-off goes to the sales exchange variances account, the same way as for a payment. The write-off is a customer transaction like the late payment charges.

My Reminders and Charges

A customer who logs in sees the reminders and the late payment charges addressed to the customer, and nobody else's.

Settings

The system parameters hold the credit review interval in months, the late payment interest rate per month, the reminder fee and the wording of the three reminder letters. The company preferences hold the two new ledger accounts, the late payment charges income account and the bad debt expense account; they cannot be deleted in the chart of accounts while they are in use there. A new installation, with or without demo data, has these settings; an existing database gets them from the database upgrade, which runs by itself from the Database Upgrade screen after the new code is installed.

Customer Credit Control

Credit control in webERP applies the same rules every time, by everybody, and leaves a trail the auditors can follow. It covers credit reviews, holding and releasing accounts, overdue reminders, late payment charges and the write-off of bad debt. The screens are on the Receivables menus. Only the credit controller and the deputy - the users whose security role holds the security token Credit control - reviews, holds, reminders, charges and write-offs (token 21) - can change anything. A new database gives the token to the System Administrator role; give it to the role of the credit controller in the Access Permissions Maintenance screen. Everyone else with access to customers can look at the credit status, the reviews and the history but not change them.

Sales people who log in see credit information only for their own customers and their own transactions in every list and report described here. Customers who log in see their own reminders and charges only, on the screen My Reminders and Charges.

Credit Reviews

Every trade customer is reviewed at least once a year - large or risky customers more often. Choose Credit Reviews on the Receivables Transactions menu or follow the link on the customer page. A review records the date, the user who is logged in, the outcome, the new limit where it changes, the date the next review is due and the comments. The comments can run to several paragraphs; quotes from the customer's emails can be pasted in. The outcome is one of:

  • Limit kept
  • Limit raised - enter the new, higher limit
  • Limit lowered - enter the new, lower limit
  • Account put on hold - choose the credit status to give it, it must be a status that disallows invoicing
  • Account put on watch - staff are warned, but can carry on
  • Account released from hold - choose a credit status that allows invoicing

When a review changes the limit or the credit status the customer's account is changed in the same database transaction as the review is saved. If either part fails neither is saved. A customer that has never been reviewed has no date and is listed as never reviewed in the report.

tool_use_result.originalFile:
Credit Status Ratings

Each customer can be given a credit status that describes the risk as assessed by the credit controller, attached to invoices to the customer. This will never appear on any reports to customers. The customer selection screen allows customers to be restricted by their credit status so it is easy to perform inquiries on all the customers with a similar credit status. In addition the system will not allow invoices to customers whose credit status has a check in the field to prohibit invoicing. This is another credit control tool to the credit limit.

Credit Status Ratings can be amended and created from the main menu set up tab from the link labelled Credit Status Maintenance.

Status Code

This is any number from 1 to 100. A rating code is required to be held against every customer to identify the credit status of each. The code cannot be changed retrospectively.

Status Description

This field is used in look ups both in the customers amendment/entry and also in the customer selection screen. This is a text field up to 30 characters long.

Disallow Invoices

For all credit ratings set up, this field indicates whether or not the rating is serious enough to prohibit future invoicing to customers set up with this credit rating.

# Customer credit control - notes

**Not run.** This environment had no shell, PHP or database, so nothing here has been executed, linted or
tested. Everything was written by reading the surrounding code and copying its patterns. Run the upgrade on a copy
of the database and exercise each screen before relying on it.

## What was added

### Schema, install and upgrade (BRD 8.1)
- `sql/updates/44.php` - the upgrade (runs from the normal Database Upgrade screen, no hand SQL). It uses only the
  existing per-database helper functions (`CreateTable`, `AddColumn`, `NewScript`, `NewMenuItem`, ...). New tables are created
  with the character set of `debtorsmaster` so the foreign keys work.
- `install/sql/tables/`: `creditreviews`, `creditreminders`, `creditreminderitems`, `creditcharges`,
  `creditwriteoffs`; new columns `debtorsmaster.nextreviewdate`, `companies.latechargeact`, `companies.baddebtact`.
- `install/sql/data/*.sql` and `install/sql/demo.sql` (fresh install with and without demo data): config rows, scripts,
  menu items, security token 21, systypes 13 and 14. The positional `INSERT INTO companies` in
  `includes/InstallFunctions.php` and in `demo.sql` got the two new columns. (The old root `sql/demo.sql` was not touched; it is not used by the installer.)
- Transaction types: **13 Late Payment Charge** (a debit) and **14 Bad Debt Write-off** (a credit).
- Security token **21** "Credit control". The upgrade gives it to role 8 (System Administrator) only - give it to
  Maria's role in Access Permissions. Menu rows are added for every existing role as other upgrades do; the pages
  themselves are token-protected.

### Screens (all on the Receivables menus; help links open `doc/Manual/ManualCreditControl.html`)
| Script | Token | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `CreditReviews.php` | 21 | record a review; review + customer limit/hold/next review date saved in one DB transaction (`FOR UPDATE`, all queries trap-and-rollback); mark a review as entered by mistake |
| `CreditHistory.php` | 2 | read-only history: reviews (newest first), reminders with invoices, charges, write-offs; linked from the customer page |
| `CreditReviewReport.php` | 2 | due/overdue/never-reviewed list with balance, overdue amount, limit, credit available, last paid; PDF |
| `CreditReminders.php` | 21 | preview who gets which level, untick, send; PDF letter emailed to statement contacts |
| `LateCharges.php` | 21 | preview and make month-end interest and reminder-fee charges; GL tags |
| `BadDebtWriteOff.php` | 21 | write off chosen items or the whole balance |
| `PrintCustCharge.php` | 2 | PDF / email of a charge |
| `CustomerCreditNotices.php` | 1 | customer login sees own reminders and charges |

`includes/CreditControlFunctions.php` holds the shared code (hold status lookup, past-due SQL, salesperson filters, letter/PDF/email helpers).

### Changes to existing code
- **Hold, all routes (2.1):** recurring orders (`RecurringSalesOrdersProcess.php`, skipped and left due), invoicing of
  entered orders (`ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php`, at load and again at "Process Invoice"), EDI orders
  (`EDIProcessOrders.php`), web-shop API order insert and `InvoiceSalesOrder` (`api/includes/api_salesorders.php`),
  order placement (`DeliveryDetails.php`, in case the hold came after the order was started). Fixed `SelectOrderItems.php`: a customer
  placing their own order was blocked on *watch* as if on hold.
- **Watch (2.2):** `holdreasons.dissallowinvoices = 2` already existed and is already honoured as a warning by the
  order screens; `CreditStatus.php` could not set it, now it can (select: OK / Watch / Hold).
- **Who may change hold/limit (2.3):** `Customers.php` disables credit limit, credit status and review date for
  anyone without token 21 and ignores whatever is posted; new customers made by others get the default limit and a
  non-blocking status. Deleting a customer removes its credit history.
- **Next review date (1.3):** kept by `Customers.php` (create/edit), `Z_ChangeCustomerCode.php` (copy + re-point all new tables),
  `Z_ImportDebtors.php` (default on insert), the API (`InsertCustomer` default, validated date).
- **Web shop (7.2):** `api_customers.php` validates `nextreviewdate` as a real `YYYY-MM-DD`; `ModifyCustomer` rejects any change of
  `holdreason`/`creditlimit` and `InsertCustomer` rejects creating a customer on hold/watch (new error codes 1174-1176).
- **Ledger agrees with customer accounts (intro):** types 13/14 are included in `Z_CheckDebtorsControl.php`,
  `CustomerBalancesMovement.php` (charges are debits), `DebtorsAtPeriodEnd.php` (exchange difference of write-offs),
  and shown in `CustomerAccount.php` (which silently skipped unknown types) and `CustomerInquiry.php`.
- **Settings (8.2):** `SystemParameters.php` (review interval, interest rate, reminder fee, three letter wordings);
  `CompanyPreferences.php` (late charge income account, bad debt expense account; rejects control accounts); `GLAccounts.php`
  delete check now includes these two (and `freightact`, which was missing); `Z_ChangeGLAccountCode.php` renumbers them.

## Ambiguities and how I resolved them
1. **"Past due".** `AgedDebtors.php`, `CustomerInquiry.php` and `PrintCustStatements.php` agree: with
   days-before-due terms an invoice is past due when `today - invoice date >= days`; with day-in-following-month terms
   when `today >= last day of invoice month + that many days`. Levels 2 and 3 use the same expressions with
   `PastDueDays1/2`. I copied exactly that (`CreditPastDueSQL`). `CustomerAccount.php` calculates the following-month
   case differently; I followed the three that agree.
2. **Held customers' letters.** They get the final-notice *wording*; the recorded level is still the real level. For the reminder fee,
   a "final notice" is any letter sent with that wording (level 3 **or** customer on hold).
3. **Interest rate** is a percentage **per month** on the balance of type-10 invoices past due when the charge is run
   (not compounding on earlier charges). One interest charge per customer per month; fee: one per final-notice letter.
   Charges are dated the month end (or today if the month is not over), only this or last month can be run, no tax.
   Uniqueness is enforced by a unique key, so a repeat or parallel run cannot double charge.
4. **No double reminders.** `creditreminderitems` is unique on (invoice, level); an invoice is a candidate only when its
   current level is higher than any level it was reminded at. A letter lists only invoices not reminded at that level yet.
5. **"Correct one entered by mistake"** (1.4) is implemented as *mark as entered by mistake with a reason* (kept in history for the
   auditors, not deleted). It does not reverse the account change; record a new review for that.
6. **Existing customers** get no next review date on upgrade (NULL) and appear as "Never reviewed" in the report - they have never been reviewed. New ones default to today + interval.
7. **Comments** are required for any review that changes the limit or the status (the "why" in 2.3).
8. **Whole balance write-off** = tick every item (invoices and late charges with an amount left). Unallocated receipts are not netted. Foreign
   exchange difference is calculated and posted the same way `CustomerAllocations.php` does for receipts.
9. **Credit available** in the report uses the existing `GetCreditAvailable()` (limit - balance - open orders) so it matches order entry.
10. **2.4** untouched: `CheckCreditLimits` behaviour is as before.
11. **Customers' own page** lists reminders and charges, no PDFs; the customer is read from `www_users`, not from the session variable that the customer search changes.

## Known gaps / things I left alone
- `EDIProcessOrders.php` has `if ($CreateOrder = true)` (assignment) which makes its other error checks ineffective; I only added the hold check next to it.
- Counter sales still check hold only when the sale is started.
- Locale translations (`locale/*`) were not updated; new strings use `__()`.

8. **Whole balance write-off** = tick every item (invoices and late charges with an amount left). Unallocated receipts are not netted. Foreign
   exchange difference is calculated and posted the same way `CustomerAllocations.php` does for receipts.
9. **Credit available** in the report uses the existing `GetCreditAvailable()` (limit - balance - open orders) so it matches order entry.
10. **2.4** untouched: `CheckCreditLimits` behaviour is as before.
11. **Customers' own page** lists reminders and charges, no PDFs; the customer is read from `www_users`, not from the session variable that the customer search changes.

## Known gaps / things I left alone
- `EDIProcessOrders.php` has `if ($CreateOrder = true)` (assignment) which makes its other error checks ineffective; I only added the hold check next to it.
- Counter sales still check hold only when the sale is started.
- Locale translations (`locale/*`) were not updated; new strings use `__()`.
